title: Heterogeneous model-fit thresholds and competitive-signal decisioning
creator: Marina Alvarez
description:
Objective: Define a repeatable set of heuristics and operational thresholds that determine when we (a) recommend switching customers to a different model family, (b) surface a product alert to SRE/SE for intervention, or (c) de-prioritize a model variant due to competitive or supply-side signals.

Scope:
- Capture cross-signal inputs: model latency percentiles, token unit cost delta, eval quality regressions on core prompt sets, open-market availability (supply/release cadence), and competitor feature announcements.
- Produce a decision matrix and scoring function that outputs a single human-readable "Model Fit Score" per model-candidate for production serving per workload class (e.g., chat-short, long-context-generation, embeddings-ML).
- Define operational thresholds and recommended actions for Score buckets (Green/Yellow/Red).
- Provide guidance for automating low-risk actions (e.g., suggest quantized variant, enable caching policy) vs high-risk actions (e.g., automated rollover to fallback model requires manual approval).

Deliverables:
1) Decision matrix document (one-pager + spreadsheet) with weightings for signals and worked examples.
2) Scoring function prototype (pseudo-code + sample calculation for three customer workloads).
3) Acceptance criteria and test harness for validating score outputs against historical incidents and A/B test logs.
4) Playbook for PM/SRE/Eng on escalation and rollout when a model crosses thresholds.

Success metrics:
- Cover >= 80% of historical model-change incidents when run retroactively across last 12 months of telemetry.
- Reduce manual model-change escalations by 40% in the first quarter after rollout.
- Ensure no customer-facing latency SLO violations caused by automated low-risk actions in first 30 days (monitoring window).

Approach:
1) Signal inventory: collaborate with Research (evals), Runtime Eng (latency/cost SLOs), and Observability (console metrics) to enumerate reliable signal sources and staleness windows.
2) Weight elicitation: run stakeholder workshops to propose initial weights; translate to a configurable scoring YAML used by routing automation.
3) Backtest: run scoring against last 12 months of model telemetry and annotate where score would have recommended different actions.
4) Pilot: select two internal workloads (embedding-heavy search and multi-turn chat service) for a controlled pilot with canary routing.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Signal freshness vs noise: high-frequency latency spikes may be transient; design requires smoothing and incident-awareness.
- Business vs technical signals: marketing announcements can change supply quickly but are noisier as indicators for short-term routing.
- Weight sensitivity: small weight changes can flip decisions for marginal models; include guardrails and hysteresis.

Stakeholders:
- Product (owner): Marina Alvarez (PM lead), Connor Blake (PM assignee)
- Research: Priya Nambiar (evals lead)
- Runtime Engineering: Jayden Park (serving lead), ENG-58921
- Observability/Console: Laila Morgan
- SRE/Oncall: Mateo Ruiz

Acceptance criteria:
- Documented scoring function with examples uploaded to Drive and linked in this ticket.
- Backtest artifacts (notebooks) that show >=80% incident coverage and a list of false-positives/negatives.
- Pilot runbook and canary config committed to repo and validated in staging.

Notes on uniqueness: This effort focuses on heterogeneity—explicitly modeling per-workload fit and making the scoring interpretable for product decisions rather than a black-box ML classifier. It prioritizes operational safety and human-in-the-loop escalation for high-impact changes.
